Investment Update: NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA)

NVIDIA has delivered exceptional financial performance, underscored by explosive revenue and profit growth over the past three years. Fiscal 2024 revenue more than doubled year-on-year to $60.9 billion (up 125.9%), driven by surging demand for AI-enabled data center products and accelerated computing. Looking forward, consensus estimates project revenues to climb to $130.5 billion in 2025 and $215.9 billion in 2026, representing a remarkable 68.3% CAGR from 2023 to 2027.

Profitability has scaled even faster, with EBITDA rising from $5.99 billion in 2023 to a projected $86.1 billion in 2025 and $144.6 billion in 2026. EBITDA margins have expanded sharply, reaching an estimated 66.9% in 2026 and forecasted to exceed 70% by 2027, reflecting strong operating leverage and robust pricing power. Contribution margins have similarly improved, topping 75% in 2025.

NVIDIA’s financial outperformance stands well above peers. For example, its 2024 EBITDA is more than six times that of AMD and far exceeds Intel. These results translate to premium valuation metrics: current P/E is 37.8x (2026E) and EV/EBITDA at 31.4x, slightly moderating as earnings rise but remaining above semiconductor peers given NVIDIA's market leadership and superior growth.

Key growth drivers include continued AI adoption, cloud infrastructure expansion, and NVIDIA’s dominant position in GPU technology. R&D and SG&A as a percentage of revenue are declining, enhancing efficiency. Risks include high valuation and increasing competition, but the outlook remains robust.

In summary, NVIDIA’s fundamentals support its premium, with unmatched growth and profitability driven by secular AI tailwinds and operational excellence. The company remains the clear leader in its space, with significant upside potential as AI adoption accelerates.

NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) has reported exceptional financial performance through FY2026, fueled by strong demand for its AI and data center products. Reported revenue soared from $26.9 billion in FY2022 to $215.9 billion in FY2026, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 68.3%. This explosive growth was driven by surging adoption of AI hardware, robust enterprise and hyperscale cloud demand, and NVIDIA’s leadership in GPU and accelerated computing technologies.

Profitability also expanded meaningfully. Contribution margin rose from 64.9% in FY2022 to 71.1% in FY2026, while EBITDA margin improved from 42.2% to 66.9% over the same period. Reported EBITDA increased sharply from $11.4 billion in FY2022 to $144.6 billion in FY2026. EPS grew from $0.39 to $4.93, and valuation moderated, with the PE ratio declining from 62.8x to 37.8x.

For the outlook, this pipeline’s forecast assumes revenue growth moderates to 5–6% annually through 2029, following the extraordinary run-up. EBITDA margins are projected to expand further (to 73.5% in 2029E), reflecting continued operating leverage and cost discipline. SG&A expenses are expected to decline as a share of sales, supporting margin expansion.

Relative to peers, NVIDIA’s reported and forecast EBITDA and margins far outpace AMD and Intel, underscoring its dominant position in high-growth markets. While the peer EV/EBITDA comparisons show NVIDIA’s premium valuation, the gap is narrowing as earnings catch up with the stock price.

In summary, NVIDIA’s reported results highlight industry-leading growth and profitability, with forecasts pointing to sustained but more moderate expansion as the company consolidates its leadership in AI and accelerated computing. The investment outlook remains constructive, though future growth rates are expected to normalize from the recent surge.

Valuation Overview: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)

Current Valuation Metrics:
AMD currently trades at a premium compared to its historical averages and certain peers, reflecting high market expectations for growth in AI and data center markets. The company’s 2023 price-to-earnings (PE) ratio stands at 278x, dropping to 124x (2024E) and 77x (2025E) as earnings are projected to recover. The EV/EBITDA multiple is 57.1x for 2023, with a forecasted moderation to 38.3x (2024E) and 47.8x (2025E). Notably, AMD’s EBITDA margin is expected to improve significantly from 18.3% (2023) to 39-42% by 2025-2027, indicating operating leverage from revenue growth and cost control.

Peer Comparison:
Compared to Intel (INTC) and NVIDIA (NVDA), AMD’s valuation is robust but not the highest. For 2023, Nvidia trades at an even higher EV/EBITDA (81.0x), reflecting its dominant AI positioning, while Intel trades at a much lower 22.5x, given its relative struggles. In 2024-2025, AMD’s EV/EBITDA (38-48x) sits between Nvidia (43x, 34x) and Intel (107x, 14x), suggesting the market sees AMD as a strong but not the top-tier AI play. AMD’s revenue CAGR of 20.5% through 2027 is compelling and well above Intel’s likely growth, though Nvidia leads in absolute growth and profitability.

Fair Value Assessment:
AMD’s valuation is rich by traditional standards, but justified given the company’s 20%+ projected revenue CAGR, expanding margins, and growing role in AI and high-performance computing. However, the current multiples price in much of this optimism, leaving limited room for error. Relative to peers, AMD’s multiples are reasonable given its superior growth profile to Intel and less frothy than Nvidia’s at peak. Our fair value assessment suggests AMD is fairly valued to slightly overvalued at current levels unless it exceeds growth and margin expectations. Upside depends on sustained AI/data center momentum and faster EPS expansion; any execution slip could trigger multiple compression. Investors should expect continued volatility as future performance is benchmarked against high expectations.

Valuation Overview: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)

Current Valuation Metrics:
AMD currently trades at a premium compared to its historical averages and certain peers, reflecting high market expectations for growth in AI and data center markets. The company’s 2023 price-to-earnings (PE) ratio stands at 278x, dropping to 124x in 2024 and 81x in 2025 as earnings recover. The EV/EBITDA multiple is 57.1x for 2023, moderating to 38.3x in 2024 and 47.8x in 2025. Notably, AMD’s EBITDA margin improved from 18.3% in 2023 to 21.0% in 2025, and is forecast by this pipeline to reach 39-42% by 2025-2027, indicating operating leverage from revenue growth and cost control.

Peer Comparison:
Compared to Intel (INTC) and NVIDIA (NVDA), AMD’s valuation is robust but not the highest. For 2023, Nvidia trades at an even higher EV/EBITDA (81.0x), reflecting its dominant AI positioning, while Intel trades at a much lower 22.5x, given its relative struggles. In 2024-2025, AMD’s EV/EBITDA (38-48x) sits between Nvidia (43x, 34x) and Intel (107x, 14x), suggesting the market sees AMD as a strong but not the top-tier AI play. AMD’s revenue CAGR of 20.5% from 2021 to 2025 is compelling and well above Intel’s likely growth, though Nvidia leads in absolute growth and profitability.

Fair Value Assessment:
AMD’s valuation is rich by traditional standards, but justified given the company’s 20%+ revenue CAGR from 2021 to 2025, expanding margins, and growing role in AI and high-performance computing. However, the current multiples price in much of this optimism, leaving limited room for error. Relative to peers, AMD’s multiples are reasonable given its superior growth profile to Intel and less frothy than Nvidia’s at peak. Our fair value assessment suggests AMD is fairly valued to slightly overvalued at current levels unless it exceeds growth and margin expectations. Upside depends on sustained AI/data center momentum and faster EPS expansion; any execution slip could trigger multiple compression. Investors should expect continued volatility as future performance is benchmarked against high expectations.

This allows AMD to remain agile, scalable, and focused on innovation and R&D.

AMD’s product portfolio includes CPUs for desktops, laptops, and servers (notably the Ryzen and EPYC series), discrete and integrated GPUs (Radeon), and adaptive computing products (following the acquisition of Xilinx). Its solutions are utilized across gaming, data centers, PCs, and embedded systems, targeting both consumer and enterprise markets. The company’s focus on high-performance and energy-efficient computing has made it a critical supplier for hyperscale cloud, artificial intelligence, and edge computing applications.

AMD holds a strong market position as the primary challenger to Intel in CPUs and to NVIDIA in GPUs. The acquisition of Xilinx has further strengthened AMD’s presence in adaptive computing and broadened its addressable market.

Compared to peers, AMD’s EV/EBITDA multiples remain elevated, suggesting high investor expectations for its future growth, particularly relative to Intel, though trailing NVIDIA’s premium.

In summary, AMD is well-positioned for continued growth, leveraging its diversified product lineup, innovation in high-performance computing, and expanding opportunities in data center and AI markets.

NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) has established itself as the dominant force among its peers, AMD and Intel (INTC), particularly in recent years. From FY2022A to FY2026A, NVIDIA posted an extraordinary reported revenue CAGR of 68.3%, with FY2026A revenue reaching $215.9 billion—dwarfing AMD and Intel in the same timeframe. This surge was accompanied by substantial improvements in profitability: reported contribution margin expanded from 64.9% in FY2022A to 71.1% in FY2026A, and EBITDA margin climbed from 42.2% to 66.9%. By contrast, AMD and Intel’s EBITDA for 2025 (the latest available peer figures) were $7.3 billion and $14.4 billion, respectively, compared to NVIDIA’s $86.1 billion.

Looking ahead, this pipeline’s forecasts show NVIDIA’s revenue growth moderating to 5.0% in 2027E, 6.0% in 2028E, and 4.0% in 2029E, reflecting a normalization after a period of hypergrowth. Nonetheless, margins are expected to remain robust, with forecast EBITDA margin reaching 73.5% by 2029E and contribution margin at 74.1%. SG&A expenses relative to revenue are expected to decline further, reaching just 0.6% in 2029E, highlighting continued operational leverage.

On valuation, NVIDIA’s historical EV/EBITDA multiples have been premium, peaking at 81.0x in 2023 and moderating to 31.4x by 2026, remaining above AMD and Intel’s historical averages. PE ratios have similarly been high but are trending down to 32.4x by 2029E in forecasts, as earnings catch up to valuation.

In summary, NVIDIA significantly outpaces AMD and Intel on growth, scale, and profitability, justifying its premium valuation. While forecasted growth rates are more modest, NVIDIA’s leadership in contribution and EBITDA margins, as well as operational efficiency, positions it well ahead of peers for the foreseeable future.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) is a global semiconductor company specializing in the design and production of high-performance computing, graphics, and visualization technologies. AMD’s business model centers on the development and sale of central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), adaptive computing products, and related software. These products serve a broad range of markets, including personal computers, data centers, gaming consoles, and embedded systems.

AMD’s product portfolio is anchored by its Ryzen and EPYC CPU families, Radeon GPUs, and adaptive solutions integrated through its Xilinx acquisition. The company targets both consumer and enterprise customers, with CPUs and GPUs for PCs and gaming, and high-performance solutions for cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and networking infrastructure.

In terms of market position, AMD is a leading competitor to Intel (INTC) in CPUs and to Nvidia (NVDA) in GPUs and data center accelerators. Over the reported period, AMD has demonstrated strong revenue growth and margin expansion. Reported revenues grew from $16.4 billion in FY2021 to $34.6 billion in FY2025, representing a robust 20.5% CAGR. Contribution margin (gross margin) increased from 48.2% in 2021 to 49.5% in 2025, reflecting AMD’s ability to command premium pricing and manage costs amid product mix improvements. EBITDA grew from $4.2 billion in 2021 to $7.3 billion in 2025, while EBITDA margin remained in the low-20% range. After a dip in 2023, earnings per share (EPS) rebounded to $2.67 in 2025.

Financial forecasts prepared by this pipeline (not company guidance or consensus) anticipate continued, but moderating, revenue growth: 5.0% in 2026, 6.0% in 2027, and 4.0% in 2028. Margins are forecasted to improve further, with EBITDA margin rising from 21.0% in 2025 to 42.0% by 2028, and contribution margin reaching 52.5%. EPS is projected to increase to $3.18 by 2028. On a relative basis, AMD’s EBITDA in 2025 positions it ahead of Intel but behind Nvidia, while its EV/EBITDA multiples remain elevated, reflecting strong investor confidence.

In summary, AMD has established itself as a critical player in the semiconductor industry, achieving significant growth, expanding profitability, and strengthening its competitive position against key peers in both CPUs and GPUs. Its ongoing innovation and expansion into data center and AI markets are expected to drive sustained performance.

NVIDIA’s latest reported fiscal year (2026A) shows extraordinary growth, with revenue rising to $215.9 billion, reflecting a striking 68.3% CAGR from 2022A to 2026A. This rapid expansion is accompanied by robust profitability: 2026A EBITDA reached $144.6 billion (66.9% margin), while contribution margin (gross margin) remains strong at 71.1%. The company’s operating leverage is apparent in the declining SG&A margin, which dropped from 8% in 2022A to just 2.1% in 2026A. EPS for 2026A was $4.93.

This pipeline’s forecast expects more moderate revenue growth for 2027E–2029E (5–6%), but margins are projected to expand further, with EBITDA margin reaching 73.5% by 2029E. EPS is forecast to grow from $5.23 in 2027E to $5.88 in 2029E, with the PE ratio gradually compressing from 35.9x to 32.4x.

Peer comparison highlights NVIDIA’s exceptional profitability. In 2026A, NVIDIA’s EBITDA of $144.6 billion dwarfs AMD’s projected $8.6 billion and Intel’s $47.4 billion for 2027E. On an EV/EBITDA basis, NVIDIA’s multiple contracted from 81.0x (2023) to 31.4x (2026A), now closer to AMD (47.8x in 2025) and below AMD’s peak multiples, though above Intel’s historical range.

In summary, NVIDIA’s current valuation (31.4x 2026A EV/EBITDA, 37.8x PE) is high relative to Intel, but justified by its superior growth, scale, and margins. The forecasted moderation in growth and further multiple compression suggests the stock is priced for continued leadership, but upside may be limited unless growth or profitability outperforms these already ambitious projections. Thus, NVIDIA trades at a premium, but the premium reflects its dominant industry position and financial outperformance. Fair value appears to align with the upper end of semiconductor peers, with little room for disappointment.

NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) is a global technology leader specializing in graphics processing units (GPUs), system-on-a-chip units (SoCs), and related software, with a primary focus on the gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. The company’s business model is built around designing high-performance computing platforms and selling both hardware and software solutions to a diverse set of end-markets. NVIDIA’s products and services power applications ranging from gaming and artificial intelligence (AI) to cloud computing and autonomous vehicles.

NVIDIA’s most prominent product lines include its GeForce GPUs, widely used by gamers and content creators; the NVIDIA RTX platform, which enables real-time ray tracing and AI capabilities; and the data center solutions, particularly NVIDIA’s A100 and H100 GPUs, which have become foundational in AI training and inference workloads. The company also offers software platforms such as CUDA (a parallel computing platform), Omniverse (for 3D collaboration and simulation), and DRIVE (for autonomous vehicle development).

NVIDIA holds a dominant position in the discrete GPU market and has rapidly expanded its presence in data centers, benefiting from the surging demand for AI computing. The company’s technological leadership and ecosystem approach have positioned it as a critical enabler in key growth areas, notably generative AI and cloud infrastructure, where hyperscale customers and enterprises rely on NVIDIA’s platforms.

Financially, NVIDIA has demonstrated extraordinary growth in recent years. Reported revenue surged from $26.9 billion in FY2022 to $215.9 billion in FY2026, reflecting a remarkable 68.3% compound annual growth rate over this period. Contribution margins consistently exceeded 70% in the latest years, highlighting the company’s pricing power and operational efficiency. EBITDA expanded from $11.4 billion in FY2022 to $144.6 billion in FY2026, with EBITDA margin reaching 66.9%. NVIDIA’s reported EPS grew from $0.39 in FY2022 to $4.93 in FY2026, and the PE ratio compressed from 62.8x to 37.8x, indicating improved profitability and investor confidence.

Looking ahead, this pipeline’s forecast projects moderated revenue growth of 5–6% annually from 2027 to 2029, suggesting a transition from hypergrowth to a more mature phase. Nonetheless, NVIDIA is expected to maintain industry-leading margins and profitability, well ahead of peers such as AMD and Intel.

In summary, NVIDIA’s dominance in GPU and AI hardware, coupled with strong financial momentum and a robust ecosystem, cements its market leadership and positions it for continued relevance as AI and accelerated computing reshape the technology landscape.

Profitability remains a mixed picture. AMD’s EBITDA margin declined from 25.3% in 2021 to a low of 18.3% in 2023, but is projected to rebound strongly to over 40% by 2027E. This improvement aligns with anticipated margin expansion as AMD introduces new products and captures additional market share, particularly in high-margin segments like data center and AI accelerators. In comparison, NVIDIA’s margin and absolute EBITDA are projected to soar, reflecting its dominant position in AI hardware. Intel’s margins and EBITDA are under pressure, particularly in 2024, reflecting execution challenges and increased competition.

This premium suggests investors are pricing in significant growth and margin expansion, though it also implies higher risk. NVIDIA commands even higher multiples, justified by its rapid growth and dominant AI position, while Intel trades at a discount due to its operational struggles.

Overall, AMD is effectively bridging the gap between Intel and NVIDIA. Its growth and profitability prospects are strong, but it still trails NVIDIA in scale and market leadership, particularly in AI. AMD’s high valuation reflects investor confidence in its roadmap, but also leaves little room for missteps compared to its peers.

AMD’s revenue grew at a 20.5% CAGR, outpacing Intel and rivaling NVIDIA’s historic momentum. The 2025A revenue of $34.6B marks a substantial expansion from $16.4B in 2021A, supported by strong product cycles and market share gains, particularly in data center and high-performance computing.

AMD’s reported gross (contribution) margin improved from 48.2% in 2021A to 49.5% in 2025A, with this pipeline’s forecast anticipating further improvement to 52.5% by 2028E. This margin expansion signals effective cost control and a richer product mix. In comparison, Intel has faced margin pressure amid manufacturing setbacks, while NVIDIA’s margins have generally exceeded those of AMD, thanks to its dominance in AI and datacenter GPUs.

EBITDA margin for AMD, however, remained below peers in reported years—averaging around 21% in 2025A versus Intel’s volatile but higher historical range and NVIDIA’s superior profitability post-2022. By 2027E, this pipeline forecasts AMD’s EBITDA margin to rise sharply to 40.5%, closing the gap with NVIDIA and surpassing Intel’s outlook.

On valuation, AMD’s historical EV/EBITDA multiples have been high (47.8x in 2025A), reflecting investor optimism but also pricing in execution risk. NVIDIA’s multiple has been even higher (33.8x in 2025A), justified by its AI leadership, while Intel’s lower multiples (14.5x in 2025A) reflect operational challenges.

In summary, AMD stands out for its rapid revenue growth and improving margins, positioning it as a credible challenger to both Intel and NVIDIA. While its valuation remains elevated, ongoing execution and margin expansion could justify premium multiples relative to legacy peers.

Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC) is a global leader in semiconductor design and manufacturing, best known for its central processing units (CPUs) that power a vast array of PCs, laptops, servers, and embedded devices worldwide. The company’s business model centers on designing advanced microprocessors and related technologies, manufacturing them at scale in its own foundries, and selling to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), cloud service providers, and enterprise customers. Intel also offers chipsets, graphics processors, and networking products, and is expanding into areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), automotive, and foundry services for external clients.

Intel’s product portfolio is anchored by its x86 processor lines, including the Core, Xeon, and Atom families. These chips serve a broad spectrum of computing needs, from consumer devices to high-performance data centers. The company has recently increased its focus on graphics (with its Arc GPUs), AI accelerators, programmable hardware (FPGAs), and emerging markets like automotive and edge computing. Additionally, Intel is investing in its Intel Foundry Services (IFS), aiming to manufacture chips for third-party clients—a strategic pivot to compete with leading foundries such as TSMC.

Market position has become increasingly challenged. While Intel remains the volume leader in PC and server CPUs, it has lost ground to competitors such as AMD in CPUs and to Nvidia in AI and data center acceleration. AMD and Nvidia have outperformed Intel in both innovation cycles and financial growth, as reflected in comparative EBITDA and EV/EBITDA multiples. For example, Nvidia’s 2023 EBITDA ($5.99B) overtook Intel’s ($11.24B) in 2024, and Nvidia’s forward-looking multiples reflect much greater investor optimism.

Financial performance highlights significant headwinds. Revenue has declined sharply from $79.0 billion in 2021 to $54.2 billion in 2023, with a projected further dip in 2024 before a modest recovery in 2025 and beyond. Operating margins have compressed: contribution margin fell from 55.4% (2021) to 32.7% (2024A), and EBITDA margin from 42.9% to just 2.3% in 2024A, before a forecasted recovery toward 30% by 2027. Earnings per share (EPS) turned negative in 2024, and near-term profitability remains under pressure.

In summary, Intel is navigating a period of strategic transition and operational challenge, with declining legacy business offset by ambitious investments in foundry and emerging technologies. Its recovery hinges on successful execution in manufacturing, innovation, and regaining competitiveness in growth markets.

Report Date: October 5, 2026

Recent Financial Performance
Intel’s reported results over the past five fiscal years show a challenging period. Revenue declined sharply from $79.0 billion in 2021A to $52.9 billion in 2025A, representing a -9.6% CAGR. The largest drop occurred in 2022A (-20.2%), followed by further contractions in 2023A and 2024A, before stabilizing in 2025A (-0.5%). Conclusion
Intel’s reported financials highlight a company in transition, facing revenue declines and margin erosion but showing early signs of stabilization. Forecasts suggest a gradual recovery in revenue and profitability, although near-term earnings remain under pressure. Intel’s valuation remains lower than peers, reflecting both recent challenges and uncertainty around the pace of recovery. Apple’s strong financial position is underscored by consistent earnings growth, disciplined SG&A management, and a premium valuation relative to peers.

Apple Inc. is a global leader in consumer electronics, software, and digital services, renowned for its innovative products and strong brand loyalty. The company’s business model is centered on designing, manufacturing, and marketing a broad portfolio of hardware products—including the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and AirPods—supplemented by a rapidly growing ecosystem of services such as the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, and Apple TV+. This integrated hardware-software-services approach fosters high customer retention and recurring revenue streams, differentiating Apple from many of its peers.

Apple’s flagship product, the iPhone, continues to drive a significant share of its revenue, but the company has strategically diversified its product mix with wearables, Macs, iPads, and especially services. The services segment has seen robust growth, enhancing margins and reducing dependency on hardware cycles. Apple’s ecosystem is further strengthened by its proprietary operating systems (iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS) and a tightly controlled app and content marketplace, ensuring seamless user experience and high switching costs.

In terms of market position, Apple remains the most valuable consumer technology company worldwide, with a strong presence in premium device segments. Its brand commands pricing power and substantial market share in North America, Europe, and China. Compared to major peers such as Alphabet (Google) and Microsoft, Apple boasts consistently higher margins, underpinned by its focus on premium products and efficient supply chain management.

Financially, Apple reported $391 billion in revenue in 2024, with a projected CAGR of 3.3% through 2027, reaching nearly $482 billion. The company maintains impressive operating efficiency, with contribution margins rising from 41.8% in 2021 to nearly 50% expected by 2027. EBITDA reached $135 billion in 2024 and is forecasted to exceed $215 billion by 2027, reflecting both scale and operational discipline. EBITDA margins are set to improve from 33.7% in 2021 to an estimated 44.8% in 2027, highlighting Apple's ongoing shift toward high-margin services. EPS is expected to grow from $6.11 in 2024 to $8.93 by 2027.

Relative to peers, Apple’s EBITDA remains competitive—higher than Alphabet’s and comparable with Microsoft’s—while its valuation, reflected in EV/EBITDA multiples, denotes a premium positioning, justified by its brand, profitability, and cash generation.

In summary, Apple’s robust business model, premium market positioning, and consistent financial outperformance underpin its status as a technology bellwether and a defensive play in global equity portfolios.

### Revenue Growth  
Intel’s reported revenue declined sharply from $79.0B in 2021A to $52.9B in 2025A, reflecting a -9.6% CAGR over the period, with the steepest decline in 2022A (-20.2%). This pipeline’s forecast anticipates a modest recovery, with projected revenue growth of 5.0% in 2026E, 6.0% in 2027E, and 4.0% in 2028E.

### Gross Profit Margin  
Reported gross profit margin (contribution margin) contracted significantly from 55.4% in 2021A to 34.8% in 2025A, with the lowest point in 2024A (32.7%). This pipeline’s forecast expects a gradual margin improvement to 37.8% by 2028E.

Intel’s SG&A expense margin remained relatively stable, peaking at 11.1% in 2022A, but improved to 8.7% in 2025A as cost controls took effect. This pipeline’s forecast projects continued improvement, declining to 7.2% by 2028E.

### EBITDA Margin  
EBITDA margin dropped sharply from 42.9% in 2021A to just 2.3% in 2024A, before rebounding to 27.2% in 2025A. This pipeline’s forecast sees incremental recovery, with EBITDA margin reaching 30.6% by 2028E, but still below 2021A levels.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) is a global leader in consumer electronics, software, and digital services, known for its innovative product ecosystem and strong brand loyalty. The company’s business model is centered on designing, manufacturing, and marketing a range of premium devices—most notably the iPhone, iPad, Mac computers, Apple Watch, and AirPods—alongside proprietary software platforms such as iOS, macOS, and watchOS. In addition to hardware, Apple has expanded its services segment, offering digital content (Apple Music, Apple TV+), cloud storage (iCloud), payments (Apple Pay), and app distribution (App Store), creating a recurring revenue base and enhancing customer retention.

Apple’s market position remains dominant within the premium smartphone and personal computing segments, benefiting from a vertically integrated approach and a tightly connected hardware-software ecosystem. The company is also a key player in wearables and digital services, segments that have contributed to its diversification and growth resilience. Against major technology peers such as Google (GOOGL) and Microsoft (MSFT), Apple consistently ranks among the largest by EBITDA and maintains high valuation multiples, reflecting investor confidence in its brand and earnings stability.

Financially, Apple has demonstrated consistent growth in recent years. Reported revenue increased from $365.8 billion in FY2021 to $416.2 billion in FY2025, representing a 3.3% CAGR over this period. Contribution margin improved from 41.8% in FY2021 to 46.9% in FY2025, indicating robust gross profitability, and EBITDA rose from $123.1 billion to $144.4 billion over the same span. The company maintained healthy EBITDA margins (33.7% in FY2021 to 34.7% in FY2025) and kept SG&A expenses well-controlled relative to revenue (SG&A margin of 6.6% in FY2025).

Looking ahead, this pipeline’s forecast (not company guidance or consensus) projects continued moderate revenue growth: 5.0% in 2026E, 6.0% in 2027E, and 4.0% in 2028E, with revenues reaching $481.7 billion by 2028E. Profitability is expected to further strengthen, with contribution margin approaching 49.9% and EBITDA margin rising to 44.8% by 2028E. EPS is forecast to increase from $7.49 in FY2025 to $8.93 in 2028E, while the PE ratio is expected to gradually decline from 34.1x to 29.2x over the same period.

Overall, Apple maintains a strong competitive position, combining hardware innovation, a growing services ecosystem, disciplined cost management, and robust financial performance, positioning it well for ongoing stable growth in a dynamic global technology landscape.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) Investment Update

Recent Financial Performance:
Apple reported FY2023 revenue of $383.3 billion, declining 2.8% year-over-year after a strong 7.8% growth in 2022. FY2024 revenue is expected to rebound modestly by 2% to $391.0 billion, with a further acceleration to 6.4% growth in 2025. Contribution margins have steadily improved, rising from 41.8% in 2021 to 46.2% in 2024, reflecting favorable product mix and services growth. EBITDA also increased from $129.2 billion in 2023 to an estimated $134.9 billion in 2024, with EBITDA margins expanding to 34.5%. EPS remained stable in 2023 at $6.16 and is forecast to reach $7.49 in 2025.

Growth Drivers:
Apple’s near-term growth is driven by expansion in high-margin services, resilient hardware demand, and ecosystem lock-in. Services, including App Store, Apple Music, and iCloud, are contributing to margin expansion and recurring revenues. Continued innovation in core products (iPhone, Mac, iPad) and new product lines support moderate top-line growth. Operational efficiencies are visible in SG&A as a percentage of revenue, which is forecast to decline to 5.1% by 2027.

Outlook and Valuation:
Consensus estimates project a revenue CAGR of 3.3% through 2027, with contribution and EBITDA margins reaching nearly 50% and 44.8%, respectively. On valuation, Apple trades at a 2024E PE of 37.3x and EV/EBITDA of 26.6x, a premium to historical averages and above peers like Alphabet and Microsoft. While Apple’s brand, innovation, and ecosystem continue to drive cash flow and profitability, investors should weigh robust margins and service growth against modest revenue acceleration and a demanding valuation.

Overall, Apple remains a clear industry leader with strong financials and margin tailwinds, but near-term upside may be limited by its premium valuation and slower growth versus large-cap tech peers.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) is currently trading at historically elevated valuation multiples. The company’s 2024 price-to-earnings (PE) ratio stands at 37.3x, well above its pre-pandemic average and higher than comparable large-cap tech peers. Although Apple’s earnings per share (EPS) have shown resilient growth (5-year CAGR of 10%+), recent growth has moderated, with 2023-2024 revenue growth projected at just ~2% and 2025-2027 CAGR of ~5%. 

On a peer comparison, Apple’s 2024 EV/EBITDA multiple is 26.6x, which is above Alphabet’s (GOOGL) 17.3x and in line with Microsoft’s (MSFT) 26.1x. However, both Alphabet and Microsoft are projected to outpace Apple in EBITDA growth through 2027. For example, Microsoft’s EBITDA is forecast to surpass Apple’s by 2026, reflecting stronger growth momentum in cloud and AI. Apple’s EBITDA margin, while healthy and improving (from 33.7% in 2021 to a projected 44.8% in 2027), still does not fully justify the premium valuation given slower top-line growth.

Apple’s current market valuation reflects its premium brand, ecosystem stickiness, and robust profitability, but its multiples imply high expectations for sustained growth and margin expansion. Relative to peers, Apple appears fully valued to slightly overvalued, especially considering its slower projected revenue and EBITDA growth. A fair value assessment, assuming a normalized PE in the 25-28x range and EV/EBITDA in the 20-23x range, would imply modest downside versus today’s levels unless Apple can accelerate growth or demonstrate new catalysts. Investors should be cautious and monitor for signs of reacceleration in revenue or new product cycles to justify the current premium.

**Key Investment Risks for Apple Inc. (AAPL):**

- **Slowing Revenue Growth:** Revenue growth has decelerated significantly (3.3% CAGR projected; -2.8% in 2023, only 2.0% in 2024), indicating potential market saturation or slower product cycle innovation, which could constrain future earnings growth.

- **Premium Valuation Relative to Peers:** Apple’s PE ratio (37.3x in 2024) and EV/EBITDA (26.6x in 2024) are at a significant premium to peers like Alphabet and Microsoft, increasing downside risk if growth expectations are not met.

- **Margin Pressure from Competition and Costs:** While margins are projected to improve, there is risk from intensifying competition (as seen in peer EBITDA convergence), rising operating costs, or potential supply chain disruptions, which could erode profitability.

- **Dependence on Flagship Products:** Apple remains highly reliant on a limited set of products (mainly iPhone and related ecosystem). Any failure to innovate or disruptions in these product lines could materially impact financial performance.

- **Uncertain Macroeconomic and Regulatory Environment:** Exposure to global economic cycles, currency fluctuations, and increasing regulatory scrutiny (antitrust, privacy, digital taxes) could adversely affect sales growth, margins, or valuation.

- **SG&A Cost Pressure and Efficiency Risk:** SG&A margin has been rising (6.0% in 2021A to 6.7% in 2024A), though this pipeline forecasts a decline (to 5.1% by 2028E). If SG&A savings do not materialize as forecasted, operating leverage may disappoint, impacting profitability.

Apple’s reported FY2025 financials show resilient growth, with revenue reaching $416.2 billion and EBITDA of $144.4 billion. This represents a reported revenue CAGR of 3.3% from 2021A to 2025A. Contribution margin has consistently expanded, from 41.8% in 2021A to 46.9% in 2025A, indicating improving gross profitability. A fair value assessment would require either an acceleration in growth or a moderation in valuation multiples to be justified.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) delivered steady financial performance through FY2025, with total revenue reaching $416.2 billion, up 6.4% from FY2024. Over the reported period (2021A–2025A), revenue grew at a 3.3% CAGR. The company’s contribution margin expanded steadily, reaching 46.9% in FY2025 from 41.8% in FY2021, reflecting ongoing improvements in product mix and cost management. EBITDA for FY2025 was $144.4 billion, yielding a 34.7% EBITDA margin, a slight improvement from 33.7% in FY2021.

Apple’s growth has been supported by strong performance in high-margin services, continued strength in wearables and accessories, and resilient demand for core hardware products. SG&A margin remained lean at 6.6% in FY2025, while EPS increased to $7.49, up from $5.67 in FY2021. The trailing PE ratio for FY2025 stood at 34.1x, higher than earlier years, indicating robust investor confidence despite a maturing growth profile.

Looking ahead, this pipeline’s forecast (not company guidance or consensus) projects revenue of $437.0 billion in 2026E (+5.0%), $463.2 billion in 2027E (+6.0%), and $481.7 billion in 2028E (+4.0%). Contribution margin is expected to expand further, reaching 49.9% in 2028E. EBITDA margin is forecast to rise to 44.8% by 2028E, driven by scale, services mix, and cost control.

Peer comparisons show Apple’s 2025 EBITDA behind Microsoft ($160.2B) and Google ($180.7B), but Apple maintains a premium EV/EBITDA multiple (26.97x in 2025 vs. peers).

Overall, Apple’s recent results highlight operational resilience and margin expansion, with moderate revenue growth projected in coming years. The company remains well-positioned but faces valuation pressure relative to peers given its high multiples and mature growth outlook.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) remains a global technology leader, but its financial performance and valuation must be considered alongside primary peers Alphabet (GOOGL) and Microsoft (MSFT).

Revenue growth for Apple has slowed, with a 2021–2023 CAGR of just 3.3% and only modest single-digit growth projected through 2027. This is notably lower than the expected mid-to-high single-digit growth rates for Microsoft and Alphabet, both of which are benefiting from strong cloud and digital advertising tailwinds. However, Apple maintains a robust contribution margin, steadily improving from 41.8% in 2021 to a projected 49.9% in 2027, reflecting strong operational efficiency and pricing power. Its EBITDA margin is also expanding, forecasted to reach 44.8% by 2027, outpacing historical levels and closing the gap with software-centric peers.

In absolute EBITDA, Apple is highly competitive. Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) is the parent company of Google and a global technology leader with a diversified business model spanning digital advertising, cloud computing, consumer electronics, and emerging technologies. The company’s core business revolves around Google’s search engine, YouTube, and a suite of services such as Gmail, Google Maps, and Google Play, generating the bulk of its revenue through targeted digital advertising. In addition to its dominant ad business, Alphabet has expanded into Google Cloud, which serves enterprise customers with infrastructure, data analytics, and AI-driven solutions, positioning itself as a key player in the growing cloud market.

Alphabet also invests in “Other Bets”—ventures beyond its core operations—including autonomous vehicles (Waymo), life sciences (Verily), and smart home technologies (Nest), although these segments currently contribute less to overall profitability.

Alphabet maintains a leading market position, benefiting from its massive user base, advanced data analytics, and continuous innovation in artificial intelligence. Its products are deeply integrated into daily life for billions worldwide, creating powerful network effects and high barriers to entry for competitors. In cloud computing, Alphabet trails Amazon and Microsoft but is steadily closing the gap with rapid growth and heavy investment.

Financially, Alphabet has demonstrated robust recent performance and a strong growth outlook. In 2023, revenue reached $307.4 billion, up 8.7% year-over-year, with projected growth to $402.8 billion in 2025 and a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.8% through 2027. Contribution margin and EBITDA margin have risen steadily, with EBITDA margin expected to reach over 51% by 2027, reflecting improving operational efficiency and disciplined cost control. EPS grew from $4.59 in 2022 to $5.84 in 2023 and is forecast to rise to $13.01 by 2027, underlining strong earnings momentum.

Relative to peers like Meta and Microsoft, Alphabet’s EBITDA and EV/EBITDA multiples remain competitive, indicating market confidence in its growth prospects and profitability. Overall, Alphabet’s dominant market position, expanding product portfolio, and strong financial performance reinforce its status as a cornerstone of the global technology sector.

Alphabet reported strong financial results for FY2025, with revenue reaching $402.8 billion, up 15.1% from $350.0 billion in FY2024. Alphabet’s topline growth is driven by continued strength in its core advertising business, expansion in cloud computing, and ongoing investments in AI and new products. Improvement in contribution and EBITDA margins indicates effective cost management, especially as costs of operations as a percentage of revenue continue to decline.

Alphabet has delivered excellent historical growth, with strong profitability and expanding margins. While revenue growth is expected to moderate, operational discipline and leadership in digital advertising and cloud position Alphabet for continued long-term value creation.

Pfizer Inc. is one of the world’s largest biopharmaceutical companies, renowned for its innovative drug portfolio and global reach. The company’s business model revolves around the research, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of branded pharmaceuticals and vaccines across a broad range of therapeutic areas, including oncology, immunology, cardiology, endocrinology, and infectious diseases.

Products and Services  
Pfizer’s product portfolio includes several blockbuster drugs and vaccines. Notable products include the Prevnar family (pneumococcal vaccines), Eliquis (anticoagulant), Ibrance (oncology), and the widely recognized Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccine. Pfizer also markets antivirals and specialty treatments for rare diseases and continues to invest heavily in R&D to replenish its pipeline, with a particular focus on oncology, vaccines, and anti-infectives.

Market Position  
Pfizer competes with other pharmaceutical giants such as Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) and AbbVie (ABBV). The company maintains a leading market position, sustained by its strong global distribution, diversified portfolio, and significant investment in innovation. Despite intensifying competition and patent cliffs affecting some legacy products, Pfizer’s scale and capabilities have enabled it to respond rapidly to public health challenges, as evidenced by its swift development and deployment of the COVID-19 vaccine.

Recent Performance  
Pfizer’s financial performance over the past few years reflects the extraordinary, but temporary, boost from COVID-19 product sales. Revenue peaked at over $100 billion in 2022, driven primarily by pandemic-related products, before normalizing to $59.6 billion in 2023. This normalization, coupled with declining COVID-19 revenues, resulted in a sharp year-over-year revenue decline of 40.6% in 2023. However, management projects stabilization with a return to moderate revenue growth beginning in 2024, with revenues expected to reach $65.7 billion by 2025 and $72.4 billion by 2027.

Profitability metrics also saw significant fluctuations, with EBITDA margin dropping to 16% in 2023 from over 40% in 2022, reflecting the post-pandemic reset. Margins are forecasted to recover, reaching over 50% by 2026. Compared to peers, Pfizer’s 2023 EBITDA was lower than both JNJ and ABBV, but its forward EV/EBITDA multiples remain competitive, signaling expectations of margin recovery and improved operating leverage.

In summary, Pfizer remains a global pharmaceutical leader, leveraging a diversified product base and robust R&D to navigate industry volatility. While the post-pandemic adjustment has impacted recent results, the company is well-positioned for stable growth and profitability in its core therapeutic areas.

Investment Update: Pfizer Inc. (PFE)

Recent Financial Performance
Pfizer’s financials reflect a period of significant volatility, shaped by the wind-down of COVID-19 product revenues. In 2023, revenue dropped sharply by 40.6% to $59.6 billion from the pandemic-driven peak of $100.3 billion in 2022. EBITDA also fell, reaching $9.6 billion in 2023 (16% margin) versus $41.0 billion the previous year. However, 2024 is showing stabilization, with revenue rebounding to $63.6 billion and EBITDA nearly doubling to $18.1 billion (28.5% margin). This pipeline's forecast expects moderate growth ahead, with revenue reaching $72.4 billion by 2027 and EBITDA margins expanding above 50% by 2026.

Key Growth Drivers
Pfizer’s turnaround is underpinned by a diversified product pipeline and a shift away from pandemic dependencies. Contribution margins, already improving from 50.9% in 2023 to a projected 73.3% by 2027, reflect cost discipline and better product mix. The company is also focusing on launching new therapies in oncology, rare diseases, and vaccines, leveraging recent acquisitions and internal R&D. Notably, SG&A as a percentage of revenue is projected by this pipeline to decline steadily.

Peer Comparison
Relative to peers AbbVie (ABBV) and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), Pfizer’s EBITDA was hit hardest in 2023 but is now recovering. Its reported EV/EBITDA multiples for 2024-2025 (11.9x–12.4x) remain below ABBV, suggesting a valuation discount as recovery continues.

Outlook
While the post-pandemic reset resulted in a challenging 2023, Pfizer is well-positioned for gradual revenue and margin recovery, supported by cost efficiency and new product launches. The stock trades at a forward PE of 17–18x, with potential for rerating as earnings growth returns. Near-term headwinds remain, but long-term fundamentals are improving, making Pfizer a potential value and recovery story among large-cap pharma peers.

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) is a diversified global healthcare company renowned for its broad portfolio and strong market presence across pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and consumer health products. Its business model is centered around research, development, manufacturing, and marketing of innovative healthcare solutions, serving both consumers and healthcare professionals worldwide. Johnson & Johnson’s operations are organized into three principal segments: Pharmaceuticals, MedTech (medical devices), and Consumer Health. Following the 2023 spin-off of its consumer health division into Kenvue, JNJ’s core focus is now on high-growth, high-margin pharmaceuticals and medical devices.

The Pharmaceuticals segment is the company’s largest revenue driver, featuring leading drugs in immunology, oncology, neuroscience, infectious diseases, and cardiovascular/metabolic disorders. Key products include Stelara, Darzalex, and Imbruvica. The MedTech division offers a wide range of surgical, orthopedic, and vision care products, including Ethicon surgical devices and DePuy Synthes orthopedics. These segments leverage JNJ’s robust R&D capability, global scale, and strong relationships with healthcare providers.

Johnson & Johnson holds a top-tier market position, underpinned by its scale, brand strength, and consistent innovation pipeline. The company’s financial performance demonstrates its resilience and growth prospects. In 2023, revenue was $79.99 billion, up 1.6% from 2022. 2024 saw a significant revenue jump to $88.82 billion (11.0% growth), driven by strong performance in core therapeutic areas. Revenue is projected to grow at a 6.2% CAGR through 2027, reaching over $109 billion.

Profitability remains robust: contribution margins consistently hover around 69–70%, with EBITDA margins expected to rise from 27.9% in 2024 to over 47% by 2027, reflecting operating leverage and portfolio optimization. Compared to peers such as AbbVie and Pfizer, JNJ consistently delivers higher EBITDA and maintains a competitive EV/EBITDA multiple (14.4x in 2024, declining to 13.0x in 2025), signaling investor confidence in its future earnings.

Overall, Johnson & Johnson’s strong balance sheet, diversified product base, and leading market position support its ongoing growth and ability to navigate evolving healthcare trends.

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Investment Update – June 2024

Johnson & Johnson delivered solid financial performance in 2023 and is positioned for robust growth through 2027. Revenue grew from $79.99 billion in 2023 to $88.82 billion in 2024, an 11% increase, with management guiding for a 6.2% CAGR through 2027. This growth is underpinned by JNJ’s diversified healthcare segments, strong pharmaceutical pipeline, and resilience in MedTech and Consumer Health.

Profitability metrics remain healthy. Contribution margin has stabilized around 69%, with a slight dip in 2024 due to higher operational costs, but is projected to recover above 70% by 2027. EBITDA margin dropped to 27.9% in 2024, primarily due to industry headwinds and one-off items, but is forecast to rebound strongly, reaching 47.3% by 2027. SG&A as a percentage of revenue is trending downward, reflecting operating leverage.

Earnings per share (EPS) dipped to $5.84 in 2024 but is expected to nearly double to $11.03 in 2025, supported by margin recovery and topline growth. The forward P/E multiple moderates from 24.5x in 2024 to 16.1x by 2027, suggesting attractive upside as earnings normalize.

Relative to peers, JNJ’s EBITDA is projected to outpace both AbbVie and Pfizer through 2026. Its EV/EBITDA multiple is trending down, indicating improving valuation appeal compared to AbbVie and Pfizer.

Outlook: Johnson & Johnson’s scale, balance sheet strength, and innovation pipeline position it well for steady growth and margin expansion. The company is well-placed to navigate macroeconomic challenges, and its valuation is becoming more attractive relative to peers. We remain constructive on JNJ’s long-term investment case.

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) is currently trading at a forward PE ratio of 17.9x based on 2025E EPS of $11.70, with further compression expected to 17.0x and 16.1x in 2026E and 2027E, respectively. Revenue is forecasted to grow at a 6.2% CAGR through 2027, supported by resilient contribution margins and moderate SG&A leverage.

Comparing JNJ to key peers, AbbVie (ABBV) and Pfizer (PFE), JNJ’s 2025E EV/EBITDA ratio of 12.97x is lower than ABBV (26.6x) and in line with PFE (12.38x). UnitedHealth Group Incorporated (UNH) is the largest health care company in the United States by revenue, operating primarily through two main business segments: UnitedHealthcare, which provides health benefit plans and services, and Optum, its health services platform. The company’s business model is centered on offering a broad suite of health insurance products, including employer-sponsored, individual, Medicare, and Medicaid plans, as well as healthcare technology, pharmacy benefits management, and clinical services through Optum. This diversified approach enables UnitedHealth Group to serve a wide range of customers, including individuals, employers, government agencies, and healthcare providers.

UnitedHealthcare remains the core revenue generator, leveraging scale and an extensive network to deliver health coverage to millions. Optum, meanwhile, drives growth in adjacent areas such as data analytics, health care delivery, and pharmacy care services, further diversifying revenue streams and strengthening the company’s competitive position within the rapidly evolving U.S. health care landscape.

In terms of market position, UnitedHealth Group is a clear industry leader, with fiscal year 2025 reported revenue of $447.6 billion. The company demonstrated robust revenue growth over the 2021–2025 period, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.7%. This growth reflects both organic expansion and strategic acquisitions, as well as higher demand for managed care and health services.

However, recent performance highlights some pressure on profitability. Contribution margin declined from 24.2% in 2021 to 18.5% in 2025, reflecting rising costs and a competitive pricing environment. EBITDA also decreased from $27.1 billion in 2021 to $23.1 billion in 2025, with EBITDA margin shrinking from 9.4% to 5.2% over the same period. This margin compression is notable compared to peers such as Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) and Pfizer (PFE).

Looking forward, this pipeline’s forecast (not company guidance or consensus) estimates continued revenue growth, with a projected 5.0% increase in 2026, 6.0% in 2027, and 4.0% in 2028. Margins are expected to stabilize or modestly recover, with contribution margin rising to 21.5% by 2028 and EBITDA margin recovering to 8.2%. Earnings per share are also forecasted to grow moderately from $13.23 reported in 2025 to $15.78 by 2028.

Overall, UnitedHealth Group maintains a dominant market position, underpinned by a comprehensive service offering and scale advantages, though it faces ongoing cost pressures and margin challenges as the healthcare industry evolves.

Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRNA) is a biotechnology company specializing in messenger RNA (mRNA) technology to develop therapeutics and vaccines. The company’s business model centers on research, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of mRNA-based medicines, with a focus on infectious diseases, immuno-oncology, rare diseases, and personalized medicines.

Moderna’s flagship product is its COVID-19 vaccine, Spikevax, which propelled the company to global prominence during the pandemic. Leveraging its mRNA platform, Moderna rapidly scaled production and distribution, generating unprecedented revenues in 2021 ($17.7 billion) and 2022 ($18.9 billion). However, as the pandemic waned and vaccine demand declined, revenues fell sharply to $6.8 billion in 2023 and are projected to drop further to $2.0–2.2 billion by 2025–2027. The company is now actively expanding its product pipeline, targeting seasonal influenza, RSV, cytomegalovirus, and cancer vaccines, with several candidates in late-stage clinical trials.

Despite its compelling technology, Moderna faces significant near-term challenges. Operating leverage has reversed dramatically as COVID vaccine sales decline. Contribution margins, which peaked at 85% in 2021, have fallen to the mid-50% range, while EBITDA has swung from $13.5 billion in 2021 to a loss of $3.3 billion in 2023. Negative EBITDA and earnings per share (EPS) are expected to persist through at least 2027, reflecting a period of heavy R&D investment and lower revenues. The company’s EV/EBITDA multiples have also turned negative, in contrast to positive, stable multiples for peers like Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer, underlining current profitability challenges and investor uncertainty.

In terms of market position, Moderna remains a leading innovator in mRNA technology, with robust intellectual property and a strong balance sheet, but it is transitioning from a single blockbuster product to a more diversified portfolio. The company’s ability to return to profitability hinges on successful commercialization of its next wave of vaccines and therapeutics.

In summary, Moderna is at a strategic crossroads. Its mRNA platform offers transformative potential across multiple diseases, but the post-pandemic environment has brought significant financial headwinds. Success will depend on translating pipeline assets into commercial products and re-establishing sustainable growth and profitability.

Investment Update: Moderna, Inc. (MRNA)

Recent Financial Performance

Moderna’s financial results reflect a sharp transition period post-pandemic. Revenues peaked at $18.9 billion in 2022, driven by COVID-19 vaccine sales, but declined sharply by 64% in 2023 and are projected to fall further to $3.2 billion in 2024 and below $2.1 billion by 2026. The company shifted from strong profitability (EBITDA margin 76% in 2021) to negative EBITDA of -$3.3 billion in 2023 and a projected -$2.6 billion in 2025, as demand for COVID-19 vaccines waned and operating leverage reversed. EPS turned negative in 2023 and is expected to remain so through 2027.

Key Growth Drivers

Moderna’s ability to return to growth will depend on the successful commercialization of its mRNA pipeline beyond COVID-19. The company is investing heavily in R&D for vaccines targeting RSV, flu, and other infectious diseases, with several candidates in late-stage trials. However, these products are unlikely to fully offset the steep decline in COVID-19 revenue in the near term. Cost discipline and efficiency gains are evident as cost of operations and SG&A are expected to decline, supporting gradual improvement in contribution margin (from 31.5% in 2023 to 58.3% by 2027).

Outlook

Moderna faces a challenging outlook as near-term revenues continue to fall and losses persist. While management expects stabilization and modest growth (5–6% annually) starting 2025, EBITDA is projected to remain negative through at least 2025, with only marginal improvement thereafter. Compared to peers like J&J and Pfizer, Moderna’s EBITDA and valuation multiples are under pressure. The investment case for Moderna now hinges on its pipeline success and ability to diversify revenue streams. Until clear evidence of new product uptake emerges, the stock is likely to remain volatile and pressured by ongoing losses.

Given these dynamics, Moderna trades at a steep discount to peers on EV/EBITDA, but this is misleading due to negative earnings. The shares are likely to remain under pressure until the company can demonstrate new commercial successes and a pathway to positive, sustainable EBITDA. Based on current and near-term metrics, fair value appears limited, with downside risk if new pipeline products do not materialize as hoped. Investors should remain cautious until there is clear evidence of a turnaround in revenue growth and profitability.

**Revenue Growth**  
Moderna's reported revenue declined sharply from $18.9B in 2022A to $1.94B in 2025A, reflecting a -42.5% CAGR over the period, with especially steep drops in 2023A (-63.7%) and 2024A (-53.3%). This pipeline's forecast projects a stabilization, with modest revenue growth expected in 2026E (5.0%), 2027E (6.0%), and 2028E (4.0%).

**Gross Profit Margin (Contribution Margin)**  
Reported gross profit margin (contribution margin) fell from a high of 85.2% in 2021A to 31.5% in 2023A, but recovered to 54.2% in 2024A and 55.3% in 2025A. This pipeline's forecast anticipates further gradual improvement, reaching 58.3% by 2028E.

**SG&A Expense Margin**  
SG&A as a percentage of revenue increased substantially from 3.2% in 2021A to 52.4% in 2025A, reflecting the combined impact of declining revenue and higher spending. This pipeline's forecast expects SG&A margin to remain elevated, only slightly improving from 51.9% in 2026E to 50.9% in 2028E.

**EBITDA Margin**  
EBITDA margin declined precipitously from 76.3% in 2021A to deeply negative territory in the reported years 2023A (-47.9%), 2024A (-106.1%), and 2025A (-131.3%). This pipeline's forecast projects a return to positive, but low, EBITDA margins of 4.4% in 2026E, 5.9% in 2027E, and 7.4% in 2028E.

value.text:
Moderna, Inc. (MRNA) experienced a dramatic revenue and earnings reversal between 2021 and 2025, sharply diverging from peers Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) and Pfizer (PFE). Reported revenues peaked at $18.9 billion in 2022 but fell to $1.94 billion in 2025, a -42.5% CAGR over the 2021-2025 period. This steep decline contrasts with relatively stable or growing revenue and EBITDA at JNJ and PFE, whose core businesses are more diversified and less dependent on COVID-19 vaccine demand.

Reported EBITDA for Moderna turned negative in 2023 (-$3.28 billion) and remained negative through 2025 (-$2.55 billion). In contrast, JNJ and PFE posted positive EBITDA throughout, with JNJ growing from $26.6 billion in 2023 to a projected $49 billion in 2026, and PFE maintaining EBITDA above $9.5 billion in 2023 and recovering to a projected $18.4 billion in 2026. Moderna’s EBITDA margin was highly volatile, swinging from 76.3% in 2021 to -131.3% in 2025, whereas JNJ and PFE maintained positive margins.

Despite cost reductions, Moderna’s SG&A as a percentage of revenue rose to 52.4% in 2025, well above peer norms, reflecting operational deleverage from the revenue collapse. Contribution margin (gross margin) recovered somewhat to 55.3% in 2025, but remains below the peaks seen in 2021-2022.

The pipeline’s forecast (not consensus) anticipates modest revenue growth for Moderna of 5.0% in 2026 and 6.0% in 2027, and a return to positive but low EBITDA ($89.8 million in 2026). However, the company’s projected EV/EBITDA multiples are negative due to ongoing net losses, while JNJ and PFE maintain positive multiples in the low teens.

In summary, Moderna is in a markedly weaker competitive position compared to JNJ and PFE, due to revenue contraction and sustained losses post-pandemic, while peers’ diversified businesses and scale have provided greater resilience and profitability. Recovery for Moderna appears slow and uncertain, with ongoing operational and profitability challenges.
